title: Resolving a merge conflict
summary: Exercise 4: when two branches changed the same line.

say.never: Imagine two people editing the same sentence of a shared recipe at the same time. One changes "1 cup of sugar" to "2 cups", the other to "half a cup". Git can't guess which you want, so it stops and asks *you* to choose. That's a **merge conflict**. It's not an error, just git asking a question.
say.bit: A conflict means two branches changed the same lines differently, so git asks you to choose.

board.code:
branch A:   sugar: 2 cups
branch B:   sugar: half a cup

merge ->  CONFLICT: which one do you want?

steps.title: In your lesson: Why conflicts happen

say.never: Both `develop` and `issue-9-max-speed` changed the same line, `MAX_SPEED`, to *different* numbers. Git can't guess which one is right, so it stops and asks *you* to choose. That's a **merge conflict**. It's not an error, just git asking a question.
say.bit: Both `develop` and `issue-9-max-speed` changed `MAX_SPEED`, to different values. Git can't guess which you want, so it stops and asks you.

say.never: Open **Source Control** (the branch icon on the left). Each exercise folder has its own section there. Click **04-merge-conflict** so the buttons and menus work on that folder.
say.bit: In Source Control, click **04-merge-conflict** so the buttons act on it.

say.never: Check the branch name in the bottom-left says `develop`. Then open the **...** menu in Source Control, choose **Branch**, then **Merge...**, and pick `issue-9-max-speed`. Git reports a **conflict**, and `Constants.java` appears under **Merge Changes**.
say.bit: On `develop`: **...** menu, Branch, Merge..., `issue-9-max-speed`. Git reports a conflict in `Constants.java`.

hint.never: start the merge and see the conflict.
hint.bit: start the merge and see the conflict.

say.never: Git puts **both** versions into the file, fenced off with markers. The part between `<<<<<<<` and `=======` is what's on your branch. The part between `=======` and `>>>>>>>` is what's coming in. Your job is to keep the right one and delete the markers.
say.bit: Git writes both versions between conflict markers; keep the right one and delete the markers.

board.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
    sugar: 2 cups
=======
    sugar: half a cup
>>>>>>> issue-3-less-sugar

say.never: Git puts **both** versions into the file, fenced off with markers. The part between `<<<<<<<` and `=======` is what's on your branch. The part between `=======` and `>>>>>>>` is what's coming in. Your job is to keep the right one and delete the markers.
say.bit: Git writes **both** versions into the file, fenced off with markers.

board.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
    public static final double MAX_SPEED = 4.5;
=======
    public static final double MAX_SPEED = 5.2;
>>>>>>> issue-9-max-speed

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `Constants`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Constants` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: The editor makes this easy. Just above the conflict you'll see three little links: **Accept Current Change**, **Accept Incoming Change**, **Accept Both Changes**. Click the one that gives the right value for `MAX_SPEED`, and the markers disappear.
say.bit: Right above the conflict the editor offers **Accept Current Change**, **Accept Incoming Change** and **Accept Both Changes**. Pick one value for MAX_SPEED.

hint.never: click one of the Accept links.

say.never: Save the file. Under **Merge Changes**, hover `Constants.java` and press the **+** to say it's resolved. Then press **Commit**: the message box is already filled in with a merge message, so just accept it.
say.bit: Save, stage `Constants.java` with **+**, then press **Commit** (the merge message is pre-filled).

hint.never: stage and commit the resolved file.
hint.bit: stage and commit the resolved file.
